expect_nodes.name: POST /users
expect_nodes.note: the same CURLOPT_URL plus CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS on the same handle -> libcurl sends POST

expect_nodes.name: GET /users
expect_nodes.note: positive control: the Go chi server (GET and POST /users are two ROUTEs since LB.11a; before it they collapsed into route:/users). Measured present, so a missing ENDPOINT is a client gap, not a broken fixture

expect_edges.note: routing proof: HttpStackResolver pairs the libcurl GET to chi r.Get("/users")
routing proof: the libcurl POST pairs to chi r.Post("/users")

expect_cells.note: ENDPOINTs carry no POSITION; the call-site file rides on ENDPOINT_HIT
the verb inferred from CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS survives into the hit payload

forbid.note: exactly GET and POST /users; CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS' json argument must not be read as a URL
a CURLOPT_URL that shares its handle with CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS is a POST, not libcurl's default GET

note: libcurl easy interface, the dominant C HTTP client. client/api_client.c is C (the c_cpp row covers both). server/main.go is a Go chi server exposing GET and POST /users, so a failing cell isolates to the C client. BASELINE (0.4.18 wheel, HEAD 8155f47): the C parser emits no ENDPOINT at all, so the cell is `none`. The route control and both HTTP_CALLS pairings were verified satisfiable against this exact server dir with a python requests client (2/2 HTTP_CALLS, 2/2 ENDPOINT_HIT).
